newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil says considering buys in Moscow region.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil says considering buys in Moscow region.

text.p: Russia's largest oil producer LUKoil is considering buying into a Moscow refinery or other regional privatisation projects, the company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We are negotiating different projects with the Moscow government right now," Pyotr Neyev told Reuters.

"As for participation in the privatisation of Moscow enterprises like the NPZ refinery or other enterprises, LUKoil is considering these projects, that's all I can say. We cannot say more until we reach concrete agreements with the Moscow government," he said.

He declined to respond to comments by Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov carried by Interfax news agency saying LUKoil and Moscow, on behalf of the Tsentralnaya Toplivnaya Kompaniya which owns the Moscow NPZ refinery and Mosnefteprodukt trading company, had already had one round of talks on share swaps.
LUKoil supplies the refinery with crude and on Tuesday signed an agreement with AMO ZiL truck factory, controlled by the Moscow city government, on developing trucks for the oil industry.
LUKoil's primary goal in the Moscow region is developing its chain of gas stations, Neyev said.
